dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: ...Ow, my poor back. Why do I do this to myself? I really am an idiot.

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: Kind soul, so good to see you again! Would you like to sit awhile on my farm?

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: My back hadn't recovered from my last mishap, but for some reason, I decided to test it out against one of the tribe's best warriors. I don't know what I was thinking!

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: How should I put it? This has taught me a valuable lesson: Don't tickle your opponent's armpit when wrestling.

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: Most of the crops are growing well and I don't need to till the soil at this time of year. I just need to watch out for weasels coming to steal my vegetables.

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: What with my back being the way it is, I can't really exert myself, but luckily, I have my little Tatankasaurs to help out till I'm better.

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: Once the pain stops, I'll go help my old pa open up a new field.

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: *sigh* He's as stubborn as a mule — he's getting on in years but refuses to accept that. He won't listen to sense.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why would you even do that?

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: I'm not as strong as him. I went there to wrestle, so of course I wanted to win, but he was better than me. I had no choice but to think outside the box.

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: There we were, wrestling away, and I could see he was going to win. I was desperate.

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: Looking back, it's hard to comprehend what I was thinking. Maybe I just thought it would be funny.

dialogues.speaker: Paqarin
dialogues.text: Anyway, I just gave him a little tickle under the armpit, and in the excitement, he threw me right out of the ring!
